summary: Verified new stock-control and live Marketo Pro billing (Razorpay one-time fallback) features. Backend: 8/8 new pytest tests + prior 9/9 all pass. Frontend Playwright verified: stock display on /demo-store (honey shows 'N in stock', option dropdown shows '(N left)' / '— sold out' with disabled attribute), stock decrement after real checkout (33 -> 32 for honey), 409 sell-out surfaced via data-testid=checkout-error ('Out of stock: TEST_Tiny_7d6947 (only 1 left)'), Subscription section renders both sub-monthly-btn (₹199/mo) and sub-yearly-btn (₹999/yr) because billingConfigured=true (no billing-not-configured message), clicking Subscribe ₹199/mo calls /api/subscription/create and opens the Razorpay hosted checkout iframe overlay successfully, sub-activate-btn simulates active -> /demo-store hides data-testid=ad-slot, sub-cancel-btn restores it.

issues: Add-to-cart always inserts qty=1 lines; there is no qty picker so buyer can only oversell by adding the same product multiple times (backend still blocks with 409 — safe, just clunky UX).
Testing helpers (simulate active/inactive) are exposed to real sellers in production build. Consider gating behind an admin/env flag.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1007 lines — split into routers (auth, shop, orders, subscription, webhooks) is overdue.

create_order does the stock check and stock decrement without a MongoDB transaction; concurrent orders could race past the check and go negative. For MVP acceptable, but consider $inc with a filter {stock: {$gte: qty}} atomic update, or a Mongo session/transaction.

verify-payment matches only user.proOrderId, so a second /subscription/create overwrites the previous proOrderId and invalidates prior in-flight payment attempts — acceptable but should be documented.
Testing helper /api/subscription/simulate is unauthenticated-by-role (only requires login) and mutates real subscription status — should be behind an env flag like ENABLE_TEST_HELPERS in production.
Shop.js addToCart pushes duplicate cart lines instead of incrementing quantity — small UX gap.
